mapping_method: Preserve all154 previous mappings except explicit genuine Q18 survival additions; append all9 surviving real-core questions before any expanded answers. Separate unasked key background. Reachability credit remains separate from grading requirements.
grading_scope: Judge all actually requested material facts using equivalent wording and implied actors in context. A fixed key may include explanatory background; key_context_not_required is not an additional answer requirement or tested source coverage. A response need not recite stipulated givens or a counting guard if its answer already respects them.

creator_provenance.role: Pre-test consolidation of both independently accepted map16 context corrections

questions.question: In a two-Spirit game with 7 of 8 Fear markers already generated, an effect generates 3 Fear and earning a card exposes Terror II. Explain marker handling, new Terror timing, and when the card is revealed/resolved.

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: In a two-Spirit game with 7 of 8 Fear markers already generated, an effect generates 3 Fear and earning a card exposes Terror II. Explain marker handling, new Terror timing, and when the card is revealed/resolved.
required_facts: The eighth Fear marker earns the top card face-down, then reset all 8 markers.
The remaining 2 generated Fear go toward the next card.
Exposed Terror II takes effect immediately.
Do not reveal the earned card until Fear resolution; resolve it at the then-current Terror level.

key_context_not_required.fact: Outcome check occurs at action-tree end.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The prompt asks marker handling, Terror timing and Fear-card reveal/resolution, not a victory/defeat check.

key_context_not_required.fact: An initial stack of earned Fear cards is resolved in earned order.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The given effect earns one card. The prompt asks its reveal/resolution time and Terror level, not the ordering of an initial multi-card earned stack.

questions.question: A land with existing Blight has two Presence from Spirit A and one from Spirit B. One new Blight is added after setup. Describe Presence losses, cascade choices and what happens if the cascade enters another already-Blighted land.

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: A land with existing Blight has two Presence from Spirit A and one from Spirit B. One new Blight is added after setup. Describe Presence losses, cascade choices and what happens if the cascade enters another already-Blighted land.
required_facts: Destroy one Presence from A and one from B; put them beside the island, not back on tracks.
Add the original Blight and cascade one additional Blight to one chosen adjacent land.
If that land already had Blight, destroy one Presence of each Spirit present and cascade onward again.
Existing Blight quantity does not multiply the outgoing cascade.

questions.question: Where does setup Blight come from versus Blight added during play? When a Healthy card empties how is its new pool obtained, does the setup +1 repeat, and can removing Blight make it Healthy again?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Where does setup Blight come from versus Blight added during play? When a Healthy card empties how is its new pool obtained, does the setup +1 repeat, and can removing Blight make it Healthy again?
required_facts: Setup island Blight comes from the box; play Blight comes from the card/board pool.
On Healthy pool exhaustion flip and follow the reverse instructions, adding its printed new per-player pool from the box.
The setup +1 does not repeat on a flip.
Removing Blight never flips a Blighted card back to Healthy.

key_context_not_required.fact: Setup Blight does not cascade or destroy Presence.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The setup part asks where its Blight comes from, not setup Blight consequences.

key_context_not_required.fact: Removed island Blight returns to the currently face-up Blight Card or board pool.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The removal clause asks whether removal can make the card Healthy again. Neither it nor the setup-versus-play source question asks the destination of removed Blight.

questions.question: Explain gaining a new Minor or Major Power, including how many are drawn, where kept/unkept cards go, Major Forgetting options and the consequences of Forgetting a card already in play.

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Explain gaining a new Minor or Major Power, including how many are drawn, where kept/unkept cards go, Major Forgetting options and the consequences of Forgetting a card already in play.
required_facts: Choose Minor or Major and draw 4, reshuffling that deck's discard if needed.
Keep one in hand and put unkept cards in their deck's shared discard.
Gaining a Major requires Forgetting one owned card, including hand/discard/in-play/new Major options.
Forgotten Minor/Major goes to its deck discard; Unique goes under its panel.
Forgetting an in-play card removes its Elements and any unused use immediately.
Already resolved effects persist for their normal duration.

questions.question: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?
required_facts: Unqualified Power Damage normally hurts Invaders in the target land; it does not normally harm Dahan.
Damage from normal separate Powers can combine during the turn.
Damage reaching Health immediately destroys a piece; survivor Damage clears at Time Passes.
Destroying a Town/City causes 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear.
Remove/Replace themselves generate no destruction Fear.
Replace retains prior Damage and can cause destruction if it meets the new piece's Health.
An outright Destroy instruction eliminates its specified piece regardless of current Damage or Health, unlike Damage that must reach Health.
Remove also takes the specified piece off the board without a Damage/Health test; its no-automatic-Fear distinction remains required.
Replace removes the original piece and puts the specified replacement in its place; preserve the existing retained-Damage/new-Health-destruction requirement.

key_context_not_required.fact: An ordinary Power Damage budget may be distributed among Invaders in its target land as desired.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The comparison is explicitly for Fear and survival, followed by accumulation, Dahan recipients and retained replacement Damage. It never asks how freely a Damage budget can be split among different Invaders.

key_context_not_required.fact: Do not demand a separate recitation of the physical destination supply or destruction triggers; those are not additional survival/Fear comparison facts.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: Source-only Q18 correction explicitly excludes this background from new required facts.

key_context_not_required.fact: Do not demand a specific named-card example or new protection-effect exception.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: Source-only Q18 correction explicitly excludes this background from new required facts.

key_context_not_required.fact: Do not double-penalize a semantically complete survival comparison for failing to repeat equivalent wording.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: Source-only Q18 correction explicitly excludes this background from new required facts.

questions.question: Do damaged Invaders and Dahan deal less Damage? If Defend 1 and Defend 2 both affect a land with total Invader Damage 4, what Damage reaches the land and Dahan?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Do damaged Invaders and Dahan deal less Damage? If Defend 1 and Defend 2 both affect a land with total Invader Damage 4, what Damage reaches the land and Dahan?
required_facts: Damaged Invaders and Dahan deal their full normal Damage.
Defend 1 and 2 stack to Defend 3.
Invader total 4 becomes 1 Damage to land and separately 1 Damage to Dahan.

key_context_not_required.fact: The resulting 1 Damage to the land adds no Blight.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The prompt asks the Damage reaching land and Dahan, not the subsequent Blight consequence. The complete numeric answer is 1 to each.

questions.question: May a newly gained Growth Power be played in the same Spirit Phase? Does a Power gained in Fast automatically enter play or resolve immediately, and is there a hand-size or hand-secrecy limit?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: May a newly gained Growth Power be played in the same Spirit Phase? Does a Power gained in Fast automatically enter play or resolve immediately, and is there a hand-size or hand-secrecy limit?
required_facts: A Growth-gained card may be played later in the same Spirit Phase.
A Fast-gained card does not automatically enter play.
Gaining that card in Fast does not automatically resolve its effects immediately.
There is no hand-size limit and cards may be shown to others.

key_context_not_required.fact: Even when a separate effect explicitly permits playing a card, that permission alone does not automatically resolve it immediately.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The prompt asks about a newly gained Power. It does not stipulate an effect explicitly playing that card; that is the separate premise of Q38.

key_context_not_required.fact: A newly gained Power normally goes to hand.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: Q37 asks same-phase play eligibility and automatic play/resolution, not its destination. Q17 directly asks the destination.

questions.question: When a Fast Gift of Strength or Powerstorm grants a Repeat, must the card be chosen immediately? Can the chosen card be Slow, can it be an innate, and do you gain its printed Elements again?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: When a Fast Gift of Strength or Powerstorm grants a Repeat, must the card be chosen immediately? Can the chosen card be Slow, can it be an innate, and do you gain its printed Elements again?
required_facts: Choose a card for the granted Repeat when actually using the option, not necessarily when granted.
A Slow card can be chosen and repeated in Slow.
Gift of Strength/Powerstorm say Power Card and cannot repeat an Innate.
Repeating does not grant printed card Elements again.

key_context_not_required.fact: Explicit Elements in repeated text are granted again.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: It asks printed Elements, not a repeated explicit grant of Elements.

questions.question: What happens when Powerstorm itself is Repeated, and can its threshold spend all three Repeat permissions on the same Power Card?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: What happens when Powerstorm itself is Repeated, and can its threshold spend all three Repeat permissions on the same Power Card?
required_facts: Ignore Repeat instructions when repeating Powerstorm; it grants no further Repeat permissions.
Its non-Repeat Energy gain still resolves.
Its threshold permits up to three different cards, not three repetitions of the same card.

questions.question: What does the Coastal Lands Invader card affect when Exploring, Building and Ravaging, and do its Build/Ravage effects bypass usual requirements?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: What does the Coastal Lands Invader card affect when Exploring, Building and Ravaging, and do its Build/Ravage effects bypass usual requirements?
required_facts: Coastal Lands affects all Coastal lands on all boards for Explore and its later Build/Ravage.
Ordinary requirements still apply to Build/Ravage; it does not bypass Invader presence requirements.
Explore requires sources, with the Ocean providing coastal access.

questions.question: After Invader cards advance, can Slow Powers remove a newly added Explorer to prevent a future Build, or has it already Built? When does Fear from a Slow Power normally resolve?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: After Invader cards advance, can Slow Powers remove a newly added Explorer to prevent a future Build, or has it already Built? When does Fear from a Slow Power normally resolve?
required_facts: The just-added Explorer has only Explored; the card is in Build for next turn.
A Slow Power may remove it before then and thereby prevent a future Build if no Invaders remain.
Fear cards earned in Slow normally resolve in the next Invader Phase's Fear step.

questions.question: An effect removes two Invaders in a land with two Cities. Must Explorers be removed first, and if a card instead allows removing a number of Health worth, does existing Damage reduce that Health?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: An effect removes two Invaders in a land with two Cities. Must Explorers be removed first, and if a card instead allows removing a number of Health worth, does existing Damage reduce that Health?
required_facts: Remove two Invaders can remove both Cities; no Explorer-first rule applies.
Marked Damage does not reduce Health for that allowance.

key_context_not_required.fact: A Health-based removal allowance uses current Health, including any Health modifiers.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The Health subquestion specifically asks whether already marked Damage reduces Health. It supplies no Health modifier and does not ask modifier handling.

questions.question: Can Bringer deal real Damage by a Power saying Dahan or another Spirit deals it? Contrast Fear Cards, counterattacks after its Defend, removing/replacing Invaders, and adding Blight.

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Can Bringer deal real Damage by a Power saying Dahan or another Spirit deals it? Contrast Fear Cards, counterattacks after its Defend, removing/replacing Invaders, and adding Blight.
required_facts: Bringer's Power's explicit Damage/Destroy remains hypothetical even if it says Dahan or another Spirit deals it.
Fear Cards deal real Damage and Dahan Ravage counterattacks remain real after Bringer's Defend.
Bringer can Remove/Replace Invaders.
Bringer can add real Blight, which destroys Presence normally.

questions.question: Can a Spirit give its unused Energy or Card Plays to another Spirit, or save unused Card Plays for the next turn? How does this differ from an explicit Power that grants another Spirit Energy or an extra play?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: Can a Spirit give its unused Energy or Card Plays to another Spirit, or save unused Card Plays for the next turn? How does this differ from an explicit Power that grants another Spirit Energy or an extra play?
required_facts: There is no ordinary transfer of individual Energy or Card Plays.
Unused Card Plays cannot be saved for the next turn.
Explicit Powers granting Energy or extra plays follow their instructions and can give those benefits.

key_context_not_required.fact: Unused Energy can carry over to the next turn.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: The prompt asks transfer of Energy/Card Plays, saving Card Plays and explicit grants. It never asks saving Energy.

questions.question: What is the order of the Invader Phase, and if a Blighted Island start-of-phase effect destroys a Spirit’s last Presence, may an earned Fear Card resolve first to avert defeat?

requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: What is the order of the Invader Phase, and if a Blighted Island start-of-phase effect destroys a Spirit’s last Presence, may an earned Fear Card resolve first to avert defeat?
required_facts: Invader Phase order is Blighted Island instructions, earned Fear, Ravage, Build, Explore, advance cards.
Complete the start-of-phase Blighted effect tree and check outcomes before Fear.
If the Spirit still has no island Presence and there is no simultaneous victory, lose before the earned Fear card can resolve.
Do not reorder Fear ahead of the Blighted instruction to avert defeat.
